title: Nvidia and Vertiv Boost AI Token Output 30% With Faster Deployment

tickers.name: Vertiv Holdings Co Class A Common Stock

summary:
A new infrastructure approach developed by Nvidia and Vertiv shrinks the timeline for bringing AI factories to productive capacity from 120 days to 48 days. This method, which combines the Vera Rubin DSX reference design with prefabricated infrastructure, can increase cumulative AI token output by up to 30% in the first year. CEO Jensen Huang warned that delay costs are extreme, noting that a three month setback for a 1 GW data center—costing $50 billion to build—can result in $10 billion in lost annual revenue. Polar Data Centers is applying this approach to the initial 41 MW phase of its facility in Norway.

The efficiency gains build on the DSX POD modular units introduced at GTC Berlin, which cut on-site installation at prepared sites from six months to as little as 14 days. These containerized systems, which integrate compute, networking, and liquid cooling, are slated for worldwide availability in early 2027 through 17 partners including Dell and Foxconn. The DSX platform also reduces power use by up to 30% per token via MaxLPS and cuts cooling water use to near zero at a 2 GW scale.

selectedTweets.text:
Jensen Huang says NVIDIA's DSX POD could cut the time from AI hardware arrival to producing tokens from four to five months down to about one month.

He says a one-gigawatt AI data center costs $50 billion and is expected to generate $40 billion in annual revenue, meaning a three-month delay could cost $10 billion in revenue.

“$10 billion worth of revenues will make anybody anxious.”

Jensen explained:

“And so by moving this into the supply chain, the speed by which we can turn on go from installation, arrival of computing to production of tokens will go from many months. We think something along the lines of 4 to 5 months down to about a month.”

“Okay, so this is a complete transformation of the world's supply chain and this will change the way that people install and build data centers.”

“And hopefully as a result, velocity goes up, the wasted idle compute, the wasted idle CapEx will reduce and everybody becomes more profitable.”
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
NVIDIA announced DSX POD, a new modular AI factory design that could reduce deployment time from six months to as little as 14 days.

The new system is built around $NVDA's Vera Rubin platform and allows complete AI factories to be assembled, integrated, and tested inside modular containers before being delivered to customers.

Instead of building everything on-site, NVIDIA's partners can preinstall computing systems, networking, cabling, rack-level power, and liquid cooling at manufacturing facilities.

Once delivered, the containers can connect to a prepared site's infrastructure, allowing companies to start running AI workloads and generating revenue much sooner.

NVIDIA is working with 17 partners to bring DSX POD AI factories to market, including:

• Dell Technologies
• HPE
• Lenovo
• Schneider Electric
• Vertiv
• Anduril
• Armada
• Bull
• Crusoe
• DayOne
• Delta
• Eaton
• Foxconn (Ingrasys)
• GIGABYTE
• Pegatron
• Quanta Cloud Technology (QCT)
• Wistron

NVIDIA expects these modular AI factories to become available worldwide in early 2027.

selectedTweets.text:
NVIDIA & VERTIV TARGET UP TO 30% MORE AI TOKENS WITH THE SAME CAPACITY

$NVDA and $VRT announced a new AI factory deployment approach at GTC Berlin that could cut the time from project kickoff to productive capacity from 120 days to just 48 days.

According to Vertiv's modeled estimates, this could result in up to 30% more cumulative AI token output in the first 12 months, without increasing installed computing capacity.

Here's how the new approach works:

• 10x Faster Design: NVIDIA's Vera Rubin DSX AI Factory reference design, Omniverse DSX Blueprint, and Vertiv's SimReady assets integrate with Dassault Systèmes' 3DEXPERIENCE platform to reduce configuration and validation time from 30 days to just 3 days.

• 50% Faster Deployment: Vertiv's prefabricated OneCore and SmartRun infrastructure could reduce on-site power and cooling deployment from 90 days to 45 days.

• 72 Days Saved: Combined, the approach could bring AI factories online approximately 10 weeks earlier, providing 317 productive days in the first year compared with 245 using conventional methods.

• Real-World Deployment: Polar Data Centers is applying Vertiv's factory-built approach to the first 41 MW phase of its AI data center in Herøya, Norway 🇳🇴, with plans to scale the facility to 100 MW.

• Factory-Built Infrastructure: Power, cooling, networking, and supporting systems can be designed and virtually validated before construction, with more assembly and testing completed off-site.
